Alternatively, we consider retraction-free search directions that line searches never
leave M≤r. In a similar manner, we adopt the framework in Figure 1 and propose
a new retraction-free GRAP-R method (rfGRAP-R). In contrast with the GRAP-R
method where all singular values of unfolding matrices are required, the rfGRAP-R
method only detects the smallest singular value of unfolding matrices, which is in favor
of saving computational costs. We prove that the rfGRAP-R method also converges
to stationary points by verifying a sufficient decrease condition in Figure 2.
In addition, numerical results validate that the proposed methods indeed converge
to stationary points, and the rfGRAP-R method performs better than the GRAP-R
method due to the simpler rank-decreasing mechanism.
Organization. We introduce the geometry of Tucker tensor varieties and notation
for tensor operations in section 2. In section 3, we provide an explicit representation
of the normal cone of Tucker tensor varieties, and propose approximate projections.
Based on two different projections, we propose two first-order methods and prove
that all accumulation points of sequences generated by these methods are stationary
in sections 4 and 5. Section 6 reports the numerical performance of proposed methods
in tensor completion. Finally, we draw the conclusion in section 7.
2. Geometry of Tucker tensor varieties. In this section, we introduce the
preliminaries of variational analysis for low-rank matrices.
Then, we describe the
notation in tensor operations and Tucker tensor varieties.
Given a nonempty subset C of Rn1×n2×···×nd, the (Bouligand) tangent cone
of C at X ∈C is defined by TX C := {V ∈Rn1×n2×···×nd : ∃t(i) →0, X (i) →
X in C, s. t. (X (i) −X)/t(i) →V}. The set NX C = (TX C)◦:= {W ∈Rn1×n2×···×nd :
⟨W, V⟩≤0 for all V ∈TX C} is called the normal cone of C at X. Note that if C is a
manifold, the tangent cone TX C (normal cone NX C) is a linear space and referred to
as the tangent space (normal space). Given a continuously differentiable function f
on C, a point x ∈C is stationary of f if ∥PTxC(−∇f(x))∥F = 0, or −∇f(x) ∈NxC
equivalently.
